title: Add verified multitape compilation, dirty frames and charged scheduling
body:
## Result

Add a self-contained Mathlib-based Lean toolkit for finite multitape compilation, completed dirty-workspace frames, and explicit subroutine costs. This is a theory and proof-infrastructure contribution: selected supplier profiles and kappa are unchanged.

The main sufficient theorem, `MultitapeToolkit.VerifiedPipeline.compile_completed_frame`, takes every actual halted execution of a fixed finite heterogeneous TM2 program of depth at most D. It constructs a literal absolute-coordinate execution in at most 2*D*n physical transitions, with exact encoded output and genuine halt. Each tape has a completed observation footprint of at most t+1 cells; matching those cells, the initial control and heads guarantees the same completed transition count under arbitrary outside dirt.

## Reusable interfaces

Thirteen proof modules supply finite scanned-symbol-only transition tables, exact relative/absolute simulation, deterministic local steps, syntax-address TM2 compilation, dependent-alphabet tagging and output recovery, unit-speed write cones, completed trace frames, protected idle spectators, and fixed-stage assembly. The implemented scheduler pays exactly sum(stageTimes)+k for k+1 fixed stages, including all k literal handoffs. Its affine volume bound and separately charged adapter Big-O lemmas can consume other contributors' concrete program and cost certificates.

A concrete three-tape/four-symbol copy program is proved universally on arbitrary dirty tapes. `API.md` gives the named interfaces and caller evidence; `PROOF.md` states the sufficient assembly and its scope. The package uses only Mathlib and Lean, with no private project imports, GPU, model, solver or oracle.

## Validation and reproduction

The publication environment is pinned to Lean 4.34.1 and exact Mathlib/dependency commits. Independent serial compilation checks all 13 proof modules. Complete defining-module auditing covers 562 declarations, including 58 private declarations and 316 theorem declarations (including generated theorem declarations), and admits only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

Mandatory real Lean controls check globally named/private helpers and reject a public axiom, an unused private axiom and a private unproved theorem. The report consumer also rejects 11 corruptions. Source controls reject missing, altered and unexpected files, including an unexpected nested manifest; optimized Python passes with the guards active. Exact task-card, Git-blob and SHA-256 provenance checks match the pinned contribution-rule snapshots.

For the inexpensive registered source/finite layer:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/multitape-proof-toolkit/verify.py --out ../toolkit-finite-result
```

That result explicitly reports `kernel_check: not_run`. It is not the formal proof replay. With the pinned Lean environment and dependency cache installed:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/multitape-proof-toolkit/replay.py \
  --lean /path/to/lean-4.34.1/bin/lean \
  --cache-project /path/to/pinned-project \
  --out ../toolkit-kernel-result
```

The formal driver rebuilds into fresh external outputs, enumerates every declaration by its actual defining module, checks the exact golden report and transitive axioms, runs the actual Lean negative fixtures, and checks source immutability. It never downloads dependencies. `VALIDATION.json` and `expected/AXIOMS.json` retain the public evidence. `ci/formal.yml` is a dedicated Lean workflow recipe; activating it is an explicit copy to the displayed workflow path. No hosted-CI or human peer-review result is claimed.

## Scope and next usable leaves

These are constructive universal implications, not a proof of the full fast multiplication theorem. The source execution premise is an actual program run; no missing arithmetic, routing or recursion is assumed proved. The finite scheduler is fixed before input quantifiers, and does not implement a variable-size recursive call stack. Input parsing, reversal, padding and canonical-output conversion require concrete separately charged adapters.

The next leaves are structured in `TASK.json`: instantiate the completed frame on an actual park/call/restore controller; implement the upstream or Mathlib I/O adapters; and build a concrete size-decreasing recursive dispatcher. Other contributors can supply those programs and cost certificates directly to the proved interfaces.

## Frontier, lineage and credits

- [PR1379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1379) identifies recursive parking, physical restoration and open Lean frame/composition work. This toolkit proves generic constructive interfaces, not its full physical caller.
- [PR1608](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1608), together with the earlier PR893 lineage, motivates exhaustive axiom-query coverage. Defining-module enumeration includes private and globally named helpers.
- [PR1611](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1611) separates finite emission binding from physical footprints and all-size compilation.
- [Lean PR1](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/pull/1) supplies the Mathlib statement/bridge context; this package supplies the complementary explicit source-to-physical compiler direction.
- [Lean PR2](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/pull/2) supplies inspected finite heterogeneous-host context.

`FRONTIER.json` pins inspected heads and dates; the initial detailed snapshot reaches PR1616. Overlap inspection includes the relevant PR sources and partial public discussion pages, not a complete census or novelty certificate. `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json` and `VERIFY.json` follow the pinned registered-package conventions; generic replay checks the source/finite layer, and full Lean validation is separate. Full upstream Git registration replay and hosted CI are not claimed.

New work is Apache-2.0, with licensing and upstream attribution preserved in `LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`. The proof implementation, review and packaging used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with three parallel Codex agents. No submitting contributor identity, credentials or private filesystem paths are included in the package.
